idiom.source: the thread-ring adapter (ids shared before start, tallies in the actor) + qb/src/qb/core/Actor.h push_forward()
idiom.note: one actor class per kind of the reference network; a value passing through unchanged is push_forward()ed in place, a compare-exchange, a joiner and a ValueDataAdapter push a new event; every hop ordered

caveats: qb's VirtualCores are pinned one per CPU from the harness's set -- the mechanism qb is built on. CAF and SObjectizer are given the same treatment through their own APIs (caf::thread_hook, so_5 work-thread factory), so the CPU budget is identical and no framework is measured with its placement mechanism switched off
wait=1 maps to setLatency(0) (busy-spin, 100% CPU per core); wait=0 maps to a park cap on a condition variable that is signalled on every enqueue
qb is compiled with QB_WITH_LOGGING enabled. Logging work emitted inside the workload window is included; the runtime log level is not inferred from the build configuration
THIS PLATFORM HAS NO REAL THREAD PINNING -- qb::CPU::ThreadPinningSupported() is false, so the placement above did not happen and the figure is not comparable with a pinned host

with cores=2 the network's steps are cut into two contiguous halves of equal message weight (bitonicsort.h placement(): the cut before step 27 of 55 at the defaults), each step whole on one VirtualCore, so a value crosses a core once; CAF and SObjectizer receive the same budget and their schedulers place every actor -- see benchmarks/savina/bitonicsort.md

qb's actor id is a 16-bit slot per VirtualCore (65 534 actors): the reference network is 44 772 actors at n=1024, 104 720 at 2048 and 241 984 at Savina's 4096, which neither one core nor two can hold -- the reason the parameter deviates from Savina's 4096; a cell whose network does not fit is declared not applicable
